overview.description: The EA52 is Subaru's first horizontally-opposed (boxer) four-cylinder engine, establishing the layout that would define Subaru for decades. Debuting in the revolutionary Subaru 1000, it featured the world's first front-wheel-drive configuration from a Japanese manufacturer.
overview.heritage: The Birth of Subaru's Boxer Legacy
overview.significance: First Subaru boxer engine, introduced FWD to Japanese market

vehicle_applications.notes: First Japanese car with front-wheel drive
Used EA61 1.1L variant, first Subaru sold in USA

notes.heritage: The EA52 represented a bold engineering decision by Subaru. While other Japanese manufacturers were using inline engines, Subaru's aircraft heritage (Nakajima Aircraft) led them to adopt the horizontally-opposed layout, which offered better balance and a lower center of gravity.
design_innovation: First mass-produced Japanese car with front-wheel drive
First Japanese boxer engine in a passenger car
Innovative front suspension with inboard front brakes
Low center of gravity improved handling
notes.reputation: The EA52 proved remarkably refined for its time. The boxer layout eliminated the vibration typical of inline fours, and the front-wheel-drive provided excellent traction. However, parts availability is now extremely limited.

common_issues.cause: Age and heat cycling degrading rubber seals
common_issues.prevention: Replace seals during any engine work
Rebuild carburetor, use fuel stabilizer if stored

notes.historical_significance: The EA52 and Subaru 1000 are recognized as pioneering vehicles in automotive history. The decision to use FWD and a boxer engine in 1966 was revolutionary, predating many European manufacturers in this configuration.
